target_name: Dear with Any of Three Risks
rationale: Adding a third arm to the gen-8 MAX union is an incremental knob-turn whose third channel (−EBITDA/LT) is largely collinear with net indebtedness, and each additional MAX arm mechanically compresses the severity leg toward its upper tail so the composite drifts back toward the expensiveness main effect (a known sales-to-price sort) rather than isolating the interaction.

The diagnosis is sound — the occupancy-count valuation leg plausibly killed the slope while producing the largest alpha — but MA(IND_RANK,5) is highly correlated with the contemporaneous rank, so this may deliver little beyond a smoothed replication of the gen-8 winner and does not truly separate "sustained" from "newly" premium firms.

The stated rationale is internally inconsistent — EBITDA/LT is a liability-scaled coverage ratio, so the claim that the signal "contains no leverage stock at all" is false and the intended clean flow-versus-encumbrance interpretation cannot be drawn — and structurally it is yet another permutation of the same MAX-union template.

This is a yardstick swap on an archive winner rather than a new mechanism, and it carries a serious construction hazard: negative-ceq firms (disproportionately the distressed names the severity leg targets) produce large negative market-to-book values that rank as "cheap," contaminating precisely the interaction being tested in a way 1% winsorization cannot repair.

A genuinely untested channel in the expensive tail with clean centered construction, though wcap/lct is essentially the current ratio and its sign is economically ambiguous among premium-valued firms, since negative working capital there often marks high-turnover, supplier-financed franchises rather than fragility.

Internally coherent and diagnostically informative about breadth versus compounding, but it changes only the aggregation operator on an existing archive signal, which is precisely the cosmetic-variant class the objective warns against; the same question could be answered with a portfolio decomposition of the existing MAX signal rather than a new evaluation slot.
